metaTitle: Electrician RPL: Fast Track Cert III (UEE30820)
metaDescription: Experienced electrician? Fast track your UEE30820 Cert III in Electrotechnology through RPL, the qualification behind an electrical licence. Free check.
heroIntro: The UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician is the qualification behind an Australian electrical licence. If you have solid electrical work experience, in Australia or overseas, RPL recognises it so you only train and get assessed where you have gaps, then sit the final practical (Capstone) assessment.
whoIsItFor:
This pathway is for people who already do electrical work but don't hold the Australian trade qualification:

  • Overseas-qualified electricians working in Australia
  • Electrical trade assistants with long, broad experience under a licensed electrician
  • Apprentices who didn't complete and kept working in the industry
  • Electrical workers holding a restricted licence who want the full trade

It replaces the older UEE30811. You need substantial, recent and varied electrical experience: wiring and installing circuits, fault finding, testing, switchboards, and working to AS/NZS 3000 (the Wiring Rules). Electrical work is high-risk, so RPL here is strict and evidence-heavy.
evidenceExamples:
Assessors need detailed, verifiable evidence of the electrical work you've done. Typical evidence:

  • A detailed statement of service or reference from a licensed electrician or electrical contractor
  • Photos and videos of installations: rough-in, fit-off, switchboards, three-phase work, fault finding
  • Test results and records you've completed (insulation resistance, earth continuity, polarity)
  • Overseas trade qualifications and licences, with certified translations
  • Payslips, employment contracts or tax records showing time in electrical roles
  • Any Australian tickets: White Card, CPR/LVR, working at heights

Expect a detailed competency conversation and practical assessments, then the Capstone assessment, which is done in person.
licensingInfo:
Electrical licences are issued by state and territory regulators, never by training organisations. In every state, the UEE30820 qualification including the Capstone (final practical) assessment is the core requirement for an unrestricted electrician's licence. Some regulators also require a period of supervised work. Regulators include:

  • New South Wales: NSW Fair Trading
  • Victoria: Energy Safe Victoria
  • Queensland: the Electrical Safety Office
  • Western Australia: Building and Energy
  • South Australia: Consumer and Business Services
  • Tasmania, ACT and NT: CBOS, Access Canberra and the NT licensing board

There is no shortcut around the Capstone. RPL can cover the units you're already competent in, but the Capstone must be passed in person. If you trained overseas, other skills-recognition pathways may also apply. Talk to us about your situation before you start.
description:
The UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician is the national trade qualification for electricians. It covers selecting, installing, setting up, testing, fault finding, repairing and maintaining electrical systems and equipment in buildings and premises, to the Australian Standards and the Wiring Rules.

It is a large qualification built on weighting points, with a substantial core and general electives, and it includes the Capstone assessment that licensing regulators rely on. It replaces UEE30811.
jobOpportunity: Solar and battery installer (with the relevant accreditation)
Electrical inspector or estimator, with experience
deliveryMode: Online evidence + in-person practical and Capstone
imageAlt: Electrician testing a switchboard with a multimeter

faqs.q: Can I get an electrician qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have substantial electrical work experience. RPL covers the units you can prove you're competent in, with gap training for the rest. You must still pass the Capstone practical assessment in person before you can apply for a licence.

faqs.q: Does UEE30820 RPL get me an electrical licence?
faqs.a: The qualification, including the Capstone, is the main requirement for an electrician's licence in every state. The licence itself is issued by your state regulator, which may also require supervised work experience. We'll explain your state's steps when you apply.

faqs.q: How long does electrician RPL take?
faqs.a: It usually takes 3 to 6 months, because the qualification is large and includes practical and Capstone assessments. Your evidence and any gap training affect the timeline.

faqs.q: I'm an electrician from overseas. Can I use RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, overseas experience can be assessed. You'll need strong evidence of the work you've done and how it compares with Australian standards. Depending on your situation, an offshore skills pathway may also be an option, so ask us before you begin.
The evidence portfolio and interview are online. Practical assessments and the Capstone are done in person at an approved assessment venue.

The cost depends on how many units your evidence covers, the gap training you need and the Capstone. It's usually far cheaper than a four-year apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check for a clear quote.

faqs.q: I studied UEE30811. Do I need UEE30820?
faqs.a: UEE30811 was replaced by UEE30820. If you completed UEE30811 it remains valid. If you didn't finish it, any new enrolment or RPL is in UEE30820, and completed units may be credited.

metaTitle: Air Conditioning & Refrigeration RPL Fast Track (UEE32225)
metaDescription: HVAC tech without the paperwork? Get your UEE32225 Cert III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration through RPL, the ARC licence pathway. Free check.
heroIntro: The UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration is the trade qualification for HVAC and refrigeration technicians, and the main pathway to a full ARC refrigerant handling licence. It replaces UEE32220. If you already install and service air conditioning or refrigeration systems, RPL can recognise that experience.
whoIsItFor:
• Air conditioning installers and service technicians
  • Refrigeration mechanics working on commercial or industrial systems
  • HVAC workers holding a restricted or split-system licence who want the full trade
  • Overseas-trained refrigeration and air conditioning mechanics

Candidates usually have several years of hands-on HVAC/R work: installing, commissioning, servicing and fault finding on split systems, ducted systems, coolrooms and commercial refrigeration, including refrigerant handling and the electrical side of the equipment.
evidenceExamples:
• A detailed reference or statement of service from a licensed refrigeration or air conditioning contractor
  • Photos and videos of installations, brazing, pressure testing, evacuation and commissioning
  • Service and commissioning records, logbooks and fault reports you've completed
  • Any ARC licence or restricted electrical licence you hold
  • Overseas qualifications, with certified translations
  • Payslips or tax records showing time in the trade

Practical assessments are usually needed for the hands-on refrigeration and electrical units.
licensingInfo:
Two kinds of licence matter for HVAC/R work:

  • Refrigerant handling: handling fluorocarbon refrigerants needs a licence from the Australian Refrigeration Council (ARC). This qualification is the pathway to the full refrigeration and air conditioning licence.
  • Electrical work: disconnecting and reconnecting equipment is electrical work, regulated by your state's electrical regulator. Some states issue a restricted electrical licence for this, with their own requirements.

Tell us which ARC licence and state electrical licence you're aiming for, and we'll check what the qualification and electives cover.
description:
The UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration covers installing, commissioning, servicing, fault finding and repairing refrigeration and air conditioning systems, from domestic split systems to commercial and industrial plant, including safe refrigerant handling and the electrical work involved.

It is the current version of the qualification, replacing UEE32220, and is built on core and elective weighting points.
imageAlt: HVAC technician servicing an outdoor air conditioning unit

faqs.q: Can I get the UEE32225 Air Conditioning and Refrigeration qualification through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have substantial hands-on HVAC/R experience. RPL covers what you can prove, with gap training and practical assessments for the rest.
UEE32220 was superseded by UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration. If you already hold UEE32220 it remains valid. New enrolments and RPL are in UEE32225.

faqs.q: Will I get an ARC licence?
faqs.a: This qualification is the pathway to the full ARC refrigeration and air conditioning licence. You apply to the ARC once you're qualified.
Usually 3 to 6 months, depending on your evidence, any gap training and practical assessment bookings.
Your evidence and interview are online. The practical refrigeration and electrical assessments are done in person.
It depends on how many units your evidence covers and what gap training you need. RPL is usually much cheaper than a full apprenticeship. Ask for a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: UEE20120 Cert II Split Air Conditioning RPL
metaDescription: Install split systems? Get the UEE20120 Certificate II in Split Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Systems through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The UEE20120 Certificate II in Split Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Systems is the qualification for split system and heat pump installers. If you already install single-head split systems or heat pump water heaters, RPL can recognise that experience.
whoIsItFor:
• Split system air conditioning installers
  • Heat pump hot water installers
  • Plumbers and electricians adding split system work
  • HVAC assistants and trade assistants

You'll usually have a year or more installing and starting up split systems or heat pumps, connecting refrigerant tubing and pressure testing, evacuating and charging systems.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of installations you completed
  • Job sheets, commissioning and leak test records
  • Your ARC licence or trainee authorisation, if you hold one
  • A white card and other tickets
  • A reference from your employer or supervisor
licensingInfo:
Two licences matter for split system work:

  • Refrigerant handling: handling refrigerants needs a licence from the Australian Refrigeration Council (ARC). This qualification is the pathway to ARC's restricted licence for split systems.
  • Electrical work: connecting the system to power is electrical work, regulated by your state. Some states issue a restricted electrical licence for it, with their own requirements.

Tell us which ARC licence and state you work in, and we'll check what the qualification covers.
description:
The UEE20120 Certificate II in Split Air Conditioning and Heat Pump Systems covers installing single-head split systems and heat pump water heaters. Core units include installing and starting up the systems, preparing and connecting refrigerant tubing, recovering, pressure testing, evacuating, charging and leak testing refrigerants, using drawings and standards, and WHS, plus elective units.

It replaces UEE20111. For full air conditioning and refrigeration work, the trade qualification is the UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate II in Split Air Conditioning through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you install split systems or heat pumps. Your installation photos, job sheets and a reference are assessed, with practical skills checked in person.

faqs.q: Will I get an ARC licence?
faqs.a: The ARC issues licences, not the training provider. This qualification is the pathway to ARC's restricted split system licence, which you apply for once you hold it.
Usually 4 to 8 weeks, depending on your evidence and the practical assessment.

faqs.q: Is this the full air conditioning trade?
faqs.a: No. It covers single-head split systems and heat pumps. The full trade is the Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: UEE30920 Cert III Electronics & Communications RPL
metaDescription: Repair or install electronics? Get the UEE30920 Certificate III in Electronics and Communications through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The UEE30920 Certificate III in Electronics and Communications is the trade qualification for electronics technicians. If you already fault-find, repair and install electronic, audio-visual, security or communications equipment, RPL can recognise that experience.
whoIsItFor:
• Electronics repair technicians
  • Audio-visual and home entertainment installers
  • Security and communications system technicians
  • Technicians who trained overseas

You'll usually have several years of electronics work: troubleshooting circuits, amplifiers, power supplies and digital systems, repairing faults and installing equipment.
evidenceExamples:
• Photos and videos of repairs and installations
  • Job cards, fault reports and test records
  • Schematics or diagrams you work from
  • Licences, cabling registration and tickets you hold
  • A reference from your employer or supervisor
licensingInfo:
Telecommunications and data cabling needs a cabling registration under ACMA rules, and work on fixed electrical wiring needs a state electrical licence. These are separate from this qualification.

Tell us what kind of work you do, and we'll check which electives fit and what registration you might need.
description:
The UEE30920 Certificate III in Electronics and Communications covers electronics trade work. Core units include solving DC circuit problems, fault-finding and repairing power supplies, troubleshooting amplifiers, resonance circuits and digital sub-systems, repairing electronic apparatus and WHS, plus electives in areas such as audio-visual, security, communications and computer systems.

It replaces UEE30911.

faqs.q: Can I get the Certificate III in Electronics and Communications through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you work as an electronics technician. Your job records, photos and a reference are assessed, with practical skills checked in person.
No. It covers electronics and communications equipment. Electricians need the UEE30820 Certificate III in Electrotechnology Electrician.
Usually 2 to 4 months, depending on your evidence and practical assessment.

faqs.q: I trained overseas. Can my experience count?
faqs.a: Yes. Overseas experience can be assessed, especially with references and recent work examples.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than an apprenticeship. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: UEE51225 Diploma of Air Con & Refrigeration Engineering RPL
metaDescription: Senior HVAC/R technician? Get the UEE51225 Diploma of Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering through RPL. Free eligibility check.
heroIntro: The UEE51225 Diploma of Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering is the advanced qualification for senior HVAC/R technicians. If you already design, commission, diagnose and maintain air conditioning and refrigeration systems, RPL can recognise that experience. It replaces UEE51220.
whoIsItFor:
• Senior HVAC/R technicians and service leads
  • Commissioning and controls technicians
  • HVAC/R estimators and design technicians
  • Refrigeration mechanics moving into engineering roles

You'll usually have several years in HVAC/R, including heat load calculations, system analysis, controls fault-finding, and installing, commissioning and servicing commercial systems.
evidenceExamples:
• Heat load calculations, system selections and reports
  • Commissioning, service and fault-finding records
  • Photos and videos of systems you installed or serviced
  • Your ARC licence and electrical licence, if you hold them
  • A reference from your employer or engineering manager
licensingInfo:
Handling refrigerants needs an Australian Refrigeration Council (ARC) licence, and electrical work needs a licence from your state's regulator. Each sets its own requirements, so the qualification alone doesn't issue a licence.

Tell us which licences you hold or need, and we'll check what this Diploma covers.
description:
The UEE51225 Diploma of Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering covers advanced HVAC/R work. Core units include establishing heat loads, analysing HVAC air, hydronic and psychrometric performance, thermodynamic parameters, selecting refrigerant piping and controls, diagnosing control system faults, installing, commissioning and servicing air conditioning and low and medium temperature systems, safe refrigerant handling and energy sector reports.

It replaces UEE51220. The trade qualification is the UEE32225 Certificate III in Air Conditioning and Refrigeration.
searchAliases: diploma of air conditioning and refrigeration engineering

faqs.q: Can I get the Diploma of Air Conditioning and Refrigeration Engineering through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you have senior HVAC/R experience. Your calculations, commissioning and service records and a reference are assessed, with practical skills checked in person.
UEE51225 is the current version and replaced UEE51220.
Usually 3 to 6 months, depending on your evidence and practical assessments.

faqs.q: Do I need the Certificate III first?
faqs.a: There are no formal entry requirements, but the core units assume trade-level HVAC/R skills, so most candidates are experienced technicians.
The cost depends on your evidence and any gap training. RPL is usually much cheaper than full study. Start with a free eligibility check.

metaTitle: UEE60220 Adv Diploma Electronics & Comms Engineering RPL
metaDescription: Design or manage electronics systems? Get the UEE60220 Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering through RPL.
heroIntro: The UEE60220 Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering is the engineering associate qualification for electronics and communications. If you already design, commission or manage electronics, computer or communications systems projects, RPL can recognise that experience.
whoIsItFor:
• Electronics and communications engineering associates
  • Senior electronics technicians moving into design
  • Telecommunications and network system designers
  • Project leads for electronics and control systems

Candidates usually have many years in electronics or communications, including designing and modifying systems, writing design briefs, commissioning and managing projects.
evidenceExamples:
• Design briefs, schematics and design reports
  • Commissioning and test records
  • Project plans and risk assessments
  • Photos of systems you designed or modified
  • A reference from your engineering manager
description:
The UEE60220 Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering covers engineering-level electronics work. Core units include developing design briefs, designing and developing electronics and computer systems projects, modifying and redesigning systems, commissioning, managing projects, risk management, WHS and sustainability, plus a large set of electives in areas such as communications, computer systems, instrumentation and control.

It replaces UEE60211 and sits above the UEE30920 Certificate III in Electronics and Communications.
searchAliases: advanced diploma electronics and communications engineering

faqs.q: Can I get the Advanced Diploma of Electronics and Communications Engineering through RPL?
faqs.a: Yes, if you design, commission or manage electronics or communications systems. Your design documents, project records and a reference are assessed.
Most of the Advanced Diploma is electives, so units are chosen to match your field, such as communications, computer systems or control.
Usually 3 to 6 months, as there are many units to evidence.
Mostly. Evidence is submitted online, and your workplace confirms your skills.
